**Next build: a Reinforced Iron Plate line (WO-001).** It's issued and ready to start.

**Why this one**
- Your two miners on the impure nodes make 60 ore/min. All of it already goes into rods and screws.
- Smart Plating is the only thing blocking Tier 4, and you need 50 of it. It needs Reinforced Iron Plate (RIP) and Rotors.
- You already have 87 Rotors and a large Screw stockpile. Nothing makes Iron Plate or RIP yet, so those are the gap.

**What you'll build**
- **Mining:** 3 Miner Mk.1s on the three unused normal iron nodes about 240–285 m NW, in the Grass Fields. Around (-516, 2294). They give 180 ore/min.
- **Smelting and plates:** 6 Smelters and 6 Constructors making Iron Plate, which gives 120 plates/min.
- **RIP:** 4 Assemblers making 20 RIP/min, using 240 Screws/min. That matches your existing screw line's output.
- **Smart Plating:** 2 Assemblers making 4/min, fed by your stockpiled Rotors. Surplus RIP goes to a Storage Container for Modular Frames later.

**Notes**
- Power draw is roughly 150 MW against your 514 MW headroom.
- Fifty Smart Plating takes about 13 minutes of runtime once the line is up.
- Leave your two existing impure-node miners alone.

Once Tier 4 is unlocked, the surplus RIP lets you start Modular Frames straight away.

answer:
**Don't build a new copper factory yet. Finish WO-001 first. Copper isn't what's blocking you.**

**What you have now**
- 1 Miner Mk.1 on the normal node at (-333, 2316), 202 m north in the Grass Fields. That's 60 ore/min.
- 2 Smelters at (-344, 2352) and (-352, 2352), making 60 ingots/min.
- 4 Wire Constructors turn those ingots into 120 wire/min, and 1 Constructor turns wire into 30 cable/min.
- You already hold 12,000 Wire and 4,800 Cable. Your whole copper line is feeding a surplus you can't use.

**Why not expand**
- Smart Plating and Tier 4 need iron, Rotors and Screws. They need no copper.
- Nothing in your base makes Copper Sheet or Quickwire.
- Sheets are mainly used for Circuit Boards, AI Limiters and Heat Sinks. Circuit Boards need plastic, which means oil, and that's a Tier 5+ step.
- AI Limiters need Quickwire, which means Caterium. The pure node is 637 m SW, so that's a separate project.

**What I'd do instead (small, cheap, no new mining)**
1. Switch off 3 of the 4 Wire Constructors. They are only filling a 12,000 stockpile.
2. Put 3 Constructors on the **Copper Sheet** recipe at the ingot output. That gives about 30 sheets/min from your existing 60 ingots/min.
3. Send the sheets to a Storage Container so they build up for Circuit Boards and AI Limiters later.

**When to expand copper**
- Add copper mining once you unlock oil or Caterium. Computers and Circuit Boards will need roughly 100+ ingots/min.
- At that point the nearest candidates are the normal nodes at (-213, 2831), about 350 m SE, and (-368, 2968), about 452 m S.

Want me to issue the sheet line as a small order after WO-001? It's about a 10-minute job.

answer:
Next iron build: a **Reinforced Iron Plate (RIP) Plant**. I've issued it as WO-001, ready to start.

**Why this one**
- Iron Plate, RIP and Smart Plating aren't automated. Smart Plating (you need 50) is the gate to Tier 4.
- You have 12,000+ Screws in storage. RIP needs 12 Screws each, so the missing ingredient is already stocked.
- You have 87 Rotors, 553 Iron Plates and 35 RIP on hand, so you can start building right now.

**The plan**
1. **Overclock the two iron miners** at (-350, 2458) and (-365, 2439) to 200%. That takes 2 Power Shards each, and you have 22. Each miner goes from 30 to 60 ore/min, which a Mk.1 belt carries exactly.
2. **Split each ore line** before its smelter. The old smelters keep getting 30 ore/min, so your screw and rotor line isn't starved. The other half goes to a new smelter.
3. **Build 2 smelters and 2 plate constructors.** That makes 40 plates/min.
4. **Build 2 Assemblers for RIP.** They take the plates plus about 80 Screws/min from the screw container at (-368.5, 2529). That gives about 6.7 RIP/min.
5. **Build one Smart Plating Assembler.** It uses RIP and your stocked Rotors. At 2/min, 50 plates takes about 25 minutes. Add a second assembler once RIP is flowing.

**Build order matters.** Your 35 RIP covers about 20 for the steps 3–4 machines plus 8 for the Smart Plating Assembler. Build the RIP assemblers first and the rest from their output.

I didn't send you to the normal iron nodes about 250 m north-west. A new mine out there means hundreds of metres of belt, and you don't need that scale yet. Those nodes are the right next step once steel opens up in Tier 4.

I haven't seen your exact layout around the smelter row. Treat the coordinates as a guide and put the machines wherever there's free ground.

When it's done, tell me what you enjoyed and what felt tedious. That decides whether the next order is more production or more logistics.

answer:
**Don't build new copper yet.** Copper is already covered, and nothing you need before Tier 4 is short of it.

**What you have**
- One miner on the normal copper node at (-333, 2316), about 200 m north in the Grass Fields. It feeds 2 smelters making 60 ingots/min.
- 4 Wire constructors take all 60 of those ingots. The result is 12,000 Wire and 4,800 Cable in storage.
- You also have 130 Stators, and Cable and Wire are the inputs for the Automated Wiring that Space Elevator phase 2 asks for. That's a lot of stock.

**Why not expand**
- Smart Plating (WO-001) uses Rotors, Reinforced Iron Plate and Screws. It needs no copper.
- No Tier 4 milestone asks for copper. They want steel, power infrastructure and logistics.
- Copper Sheets are the one gap, but nothing needs them yet. They feed Circuit Boards, which need plastic from oil, and also Heat Sinks and AI Limiters. All of those come later.

So a bigger copper mine now would only add to the Wire you already have too much of.

**Cheap prep for when you need sheets**
- Retask 1 of the 4 Wire constructors to **Copper Sheet**. It uses 20 ingots/min and makes 10 sheets/min.
- That still leaves about 45 ingots/min for the remaining Wire constructors.
- It's a recipe swap plus a storage container on the output. It takes about 5 minutes and no new mining.
- Do it once you have a use for the sheets, or when you start on oil or Circuit Boards.

**What to do instead**
1. Finish WO-001, because Smart Plating is what unlocks Tier 4.
2. Then go for steel. That means coal at (pure node about 544 m SW) plus the normal iron nodes about 250 m north-west. I'll size that order once you've unlocked Advanced Steel Production.
3. Plan the real copper expansion at the same time as oil. Those two need each other. The next copper nodes after yours are normal ones at (-213, 2831) and (-368, 2968).

I haven't issued a copper order because WO-001 is still open, and you should have one active order at a time. If you'd rather start on the sheet swap now, say so and I'll add it to WO-001.

arguments.title: Plate Works: Reinforced Iron Plate to Smart Plating
arguments.goal: Build a self-contained iron plate, rod, screw and Reinforced Iron Plate line on the north-west normal iron node, feeding Smart Plating assemblers to finish Space Elevator phase 1.
arguments.objective: Mine one normal iron node, smelt 60 ingots/min, split them into plates, rods and screws, assemble Reinforced Iron Plate, and convert it with stocked Rotors into Smart Plating. Deliver 50 Smart Plating to the Space Elevator. Your stockpiles already hold the screws and rotors, so this line adds the one thing you lack, which is an automated RIP supply.
arguments.successCondition: Smart Plating accumulates in the output container and 50 are delivered to the Space Elevator, starting phase 1 of Project Assembly. The RIP assembler keeps running at about 5 RIP/min afterwards.
arguments.strategicSignificance: Smart Plating is the only thing blocking Tier 4. The same RIP line then feeds Modular Frames and Heavy Modular Frames for every later tier.

locationRecommendation.summary: On the normal iron node in the north-west Grass Fields, about 240 m NW of your position. Build the plant flat and open beside the node.
locationRecommendation.rationale: This is the nearest normal-purity iron node. Both impure nodes close to base already have your miners on them. The two normal nodes next to it at (-516, 2294) and (-541, 2294) are free for expansion.
locationRecommendation.relativeToPlayer: About 240 m NW of you, in the north-west Grass Fields.

resourceNodes.notes: Mine this node first. One Miner Mk.1 gives 60 ore/min, which is exactly what the 2 smelters need.
Reserve for doubling the line later. Do not build on it now.

buildSteps.title: Gather materials from storage
buildSteps.description: You are carrying 35 Reinforced Iron Plate and the build needs 34. You are also carrying 553 plates, 329 cable, 394 wire and 208 concrete. Take 1 Portable Miner from the container at the HUB (-398, 2455). Take 50 Rotors from the container at (-344, 2542).

buildSteps.title: Mine and smelt
buildSteps.description: Place the miner on the normal node. Belt the ore to a splitter feeding 2 smelters side by side. Merge the smelter outputs onto one ingot belt.

buildables.name: Miner Mk.1
buildables.notes: On the normal iron node at (-490.8, 2317.1).

buildables.name: Conveyor Splitter
buildables.notes: Ore to the 2 smelters.

buildables.name: Conveyor Merger
buildables.notes: Joins the 2 smelter outputs.

buildables.name: Power Pole Mk.1
buildables.notes: Chain back to your main grid. You have 514 MW of headroom and the plant draws under 100 MW.

buildSteps.title: Plates, rods and screws
buildSteps.description: Split the ingot belt. About 45 ingots/min go to the 2 plate constructors, and the rest go to the rod constructor. Rods go to 2 screw constructors. Overflow backs up on the splitters, so nothing is wasted.

buildables.name: Conveyor Splitter
buildables.notes: One splits ingots between plates and rods. One splits plate ingots between the 2 plate constructors. One splits rods between the 2 screw constructors.

buildables.name: Conveyor Merger
buildables.notes: One merges the plate outputs. One merges the screw outputs.

buildSteps.title: Reinforced Iron Plate assembler
buildSteps.description: Feed plates and screws into one Assembler. It makes 5 RIP/min and uses 30 plates/min and 60 screws/min.

buildSteps.title: Smart Plating assemblers and storage
buildSteps.description: Split RIP between 2 Smart Plating assemblers. Feed Rotors from a container through a splitter. Merge the outputs into a second container. Fill the Rotor container with 50 or more Rotors.

buildables.name: Conveyor Splitter
buildables.notes: One splits RIP to the 2 assemblers. One splits Rotors from the input container.

buildables.name: Conveyor Merger
buildables.notes: Joins the 2 Smart Plating outputs.

I've issued **WO-001: Plate Works**. It's ready to start.

**What it builds:** a small iron plant on the normal iron node in the north-west Grass Fields, at about (-490, 2317). That's roughly 240 m NW of you.

- Smart Plating is the only thing blocking Tier 4. You need 50 for Space Elevator phase 1.

- Both iron nodes near base already have your miners on them. This is the nearest free normal-purity node.

- 1 Miner Mk.1 → 2 Smelters → 2 Iron Plate constructors, 1 Iron Rod constructor and 2 Screw constructors → 1 Assembler making Reinforced Iron Plate → 2 Assemblers making Smart Plating.
- It's self-contained, so it won't drain your screw stockpile.
- One normal-node miner gives 60 ore/min, which is exactly what the 2 smelters use.
- It makes 5 RIP/min and about 4 Smart Plating/min, so 50 Smart Plating takes roughly 12–13 minutes of run time.
- Hand-fill the Rotor input container with 50 or more Rotors from the container at (-344, 2542).

**Materials:** the build needs 34 RIP and you're carrying 35. Build the machines first and don't spend RIP elsewhere.

**Afterwards:** the RIP line keeps running for Modular Frames and Heavy Modular Frames. The next two normal nodes, at (-516, 2294) and (-541, 2294), are free for a second line.

**Side-quest:** there's an uncollected blue power slug about 80 m east of the second node, at (-446, 2291).

Start the order when you're on site.

answer:
I've issued **WO-002: Copper Sheet Tap**. It's queued behind WO-001, so finish the Plate Works first.

**What I'd build:** a small Copper Sheet line on the copper smelters you already have, at (-348, 2352). That's about 165 m north of you, in the north Grass Fields. It needs no new node or miner.

**Why this and not a bigger copper plant:**
- **Copper is mostly covered.** You hold 12,000 Wire and 4,800 Cable. Both containers hold 24 slots, and those counts look like full stacks. If they are full, your copper ingots are backing up with nowhere to go.
- **Copper Sheet is the one gap.** Nothing makes it. Hypertubes (Tier 4) needs 500, and Circuit Boards, AI Limiters and Heat Sinks use it later.
- **Phase 2 doesn't need more copper yet.** Automated Wiring needs Stator and Cable, and you already have 130 Stators and the Cable stock. It will need steel more than copper.

**The build:**
- Put a splitter on the ingot belt, then 2 Constructors on the Copper Sheet recipe. They use 40 ingots/min and make 20 sheets/min.
- The other 20 ingots/min stay on the wire line.
- Output goes through a merger into a new Storage Container. 500 sheets takes about 25 minutes of run time.
- Power draw is about 8 MW, which your 514 MW headroom covers easily.

**Timing:** each Constructor costs 2 Reinforced Iron Plate. WO-001 needs the 34 RIP you're carrying, so don't start this one until the Plate Works is making RIP.

**Check on site:** my layout data is from the 2026-10-16 save. Look at the live belts before you place the splitter.

**Later:** the next free normal copper node is at (-212, 2831), about 350 m SE. Leave it until you have oil, because that's when Circuit Boards make copper demand jump.

workOrders.title: Copper Sheet Tap
workOrders.goal: Turn the idle copper ingot supply into an automated Copper Sheet stream for Hypertubes and later circuit boards.

buildSteps.title: Split the ingot line

buildables.name: Conveyor Splitter
buildables.notes: On the ingot output belt near (-348, 2352)

buildables.name: Conveyor Belt Mk.1
buildables.notes: Branch belts to the sheet constructors

buildSteps.description: Place a splitter on the Copper Ingot belt leaving the two Smelters, before the Wire constructors. Send one branch on to the new sheet constructors and keep the other on the existing wire line.

buildSteps.title: Build the Copper Sheet constructors

buildables.name: Conveyor Splitter
buildables.notes: Feeds the second constructor

buildables.name: Conveyor Belt Mk.1
buildables.notes: Feed belts to the constructors

buildables.name: Power Pole Mk.1
buildables.notes: Connect to the existing grid

buildSteps.description: Place two Constructors in a row next to the ingot line. They use 40 ingots/min in total. The other 20 ingots/min stay on the wire line.

buildSteps.title: Collect the output

buildables.name: Conveyor Belt Mk.1
buildables.notes: Output belts

buildSteps.description: Merge both constructor outputs into one belt and run it into a Storage Container. Take the 500 sheets for Hypertubes from there when you reach Tier 4.

workOrders.objective: At the existing copper line (two Smelters at (-344, 2352) and (-352, 2352)), split off part of the ingot output into 2 Constructors making Copper Sheet, and collect the sheets in a Storage Container. Do this after WO-001, once Reinforced Iron Plate is automated. The Constructors cost 2 RIP each, and WO-001 needs the RIP you are carrying.
workOrders.strategicSignificance: Copper Sheet is the only copper intermediate nothing makes, and the wire and cable stockpiles are already large.
workOrders.successCondition: Copper Sheets are flowing into the new container and the existing Wire and Cable constructors still get ingots.
notes: The Wire container (12,000) and Cable container (4,800) both look full. If they are, the wire line is already backing up, and this tap puts those idle ingots to use.
Don't scale this up yet. Circuit Boards need plastic, which needs oil. A second copper node, at (-212, 2831) SE, can wait until you reach oil.
Source: save from 2026-10-16. Check the live belt layout on site before you place the splitter.
